description: STAN is free software for material flow analysis developed at the Research Unit for Waste and Resource Management of TU Wien under Helmut Rechberger, with the methods designed by Oliver Cencic and programming by inka software. Users draw a system of processes and flows graphically, enter measured flows, stocks, concentrations and their uncertainties, and STAN balances the system by data reconciliation and error propagation, computing unknown flows and producing Sankey diagrams at the level of goods and substances over several periods. It serves resource management, waste management and mining and metals studies at any scale, from a plant to a national economy. Version 2.8.0 was released on 26 August 2026; download requires registration on the website and is free of charge, the software was designed for Windows and has run on Mac and Linux since August 2025, and video tutorials and workshops support users. No open-source licence is stated. In September 2026 the team announced OpenSEFA, a browser-based research prototype with its reconciliation engine on GitHub. Caveats: STAN models static balances and does not simulate network dynamics. For simulation it provides material flow accounting for supply-chain and circular-economy analyses of industrial and mining systems, and for capacity planning of waste and recycling infrastructure. Related catalogue records include EXIOBASE and other input-output tables used for economy-wide material flows.
